countingRule: Atlas count includes field choices and separate access contexts. It does not count physical LCD screens or imply firmware completeness.
physicalLayout: Five columns × four rows. Digits/NO/YES in first3; A/B/C/D in column4; emergency police/fire and separate arrows in column5. Emergency buttons shown for recognition only.
criticalDistinctions: C and D are separate from left/right arrow keys.
NO advances main-menu questions and exits active options; YES advances sequential programming fields.
Record addresses and output/type codes are different namespaces.
Manager omission applies to Day Alarm inputs only.
Engineer changes commit on exit; manager/user acceptance is immediate.
Normal/High app credential flows remain fictional; no real credentials or communications.

coverage.strategy: Compared top-level flow charts, explicit worked programming sequences, defaults and value appendices across three matching manufacturer-authored V11 documents.
mappedAreas: Master Manager and restricted User menus
excludedAreas: Actual ARC, cloud, SMS or modem traffic
Actual battery loading and physical sounders
Unstated value ranges and unresolved print contradictions
coverage.confidence: Documented V11 baseline with explicit limits; not a firmware or hardware fidelity claim.

gaps.title: Duplicate printed EOL code
gaps.question: Which numeric code selects Wide range on the installed V11 keypad?
gaps.reason: Programming p19 gives code2 to both 4K7/4K7 and Wide range. Those two numeric shortcuts are not invented.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Output module field prompt and sequence
gaps.question: What display follows OP Mod Installed when your fitted output module is enabled?
gaps.reason: The guide documents output programming and module addressing but does not print the complete output-module field sequence. FINDR uses an explicitly labelled function editor fixture.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Reader and keypad code discrepancies
gaps.question: Confirm Type and Reader is value numbers on the installed V11 panel.
gaps.reason: The p21 enumeration and p22 workflow/appendix p45 disagree. FINDR uses the p21 enumeration and disables guesses beyond those named values.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Incomplete timer ranges
gaps.question: What ranges are displayed for Occupancy, Service Time and Wi-Fi Fault Delay on your V11 panel?
gaps.reason: The source omits or truncates these ranges; no arbitrary number editor has been enabled.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Fast Format-specific selection screens
gaps.question: Can you provide the exact LCD labels and channel flag cursor sequence for the Fast Format branch?
gaps.reason: The communications guide describes channel and restore flags but does not give complete screen labels. Those fields are not substituted with the different SIA/Contact ID sequence.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Alarm response stage discrepancy
gaps.question: Does your V11 Stop At selector include Confirm [4]?
gaps.reason: The explanatory stage list pp38–40 gives0–3, but defaults pp49–50 also show Confirm[4]. The undocumented stage is not offered as a verified value.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Nested attribute return behaviour
gaps.question: From halfway through Input Attributes, does NO show Input Attributes or go directly to Input Description on your V11?
gaps.reason: The guide states the general NO rule but does not illustrate this intermediate return. FINDR returns to the question before skipping it.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Predictive text and length limits
gaps.question: Can you confirm text length and C-key behaviour for input name/location and user names?
gaps.reason: The source describes multi-tap/predictive entry; only some fields have explicit length limits. The text helper uses a conservative practice limit.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Manager Day Alarm omission reinstatement
gaps.question: What exact prompt appears when selecting an already omitted Day Alarm input?
gaps.reason: The user guide documents omission and automatic restoration after set/unset, but not the full repeated-selection display. FINDR labels its local toggle as a simplified practice interaction.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Conditional communications menus
gaps.question: Which modem and firmware revision are fitted to the keypad you want to practise?
gaps.reason: The V11 guides describe different module-dependent branches. FINDR shows the documented branches with conditions and no live communications.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

gaps.title: Wireless learning, siren and test timing
gaps.question: Can matching hardware recordings confirm the complete test prompts and delays?
gaps.reason: Learning, deleting, signalling, battery loading and actual sounder timing require equipment; only local fixtures are provided.
gaps.neededEvidence: Matching Enforcer V11 software screen or manufacturer clarification.

verification.scope: Software checks validate this local simulator. Exact firmware prompts, original panel audio and physical hardware have not been verified.

importantLimits: The atlas counts selections and repeated access contexts, not physical LCD screens.
Conditional modem, reader and signalling field visibility is not a complete firmware implementation; source conditions and explicit gaps remain visible.
The module-output editor is a labelled fixture because the complete physical prompt sequence is not printed.
Fast Format channel/restore flags are source references; the fully described SIA/Contact ID field sequence must not be taken as that branch.
YES on Sound to Play acknowledges a local selection without changing programming. Exact panel tone playback and YES timing are unverified.
Learning, deleting devices, actual communications and battery-load outcomes are not invented.
Manager Day Alarm omission is distinct from ordinary input omission during arming; the exact repeated-selection restoration prompt remains unverified.
